description: Two-panel composite figure reporting tensile properties of annealed duplex lightweight steel, mixing a mechanical test plot with a materials-comparison scatter plot. (a) Engineering stress (MPa, y-axis 0-1500 with a broken axis jumping from ~450 to ~1050 MPa) versus engineering strain (%, x-axis 0-50, also broken near 5 and 48 %), six curves, legend: DP950-1 (black), DP950-5 (cyan), DP1000-1 (orange), DP1000-5 (red solid), DP1000-5-TD (dotted red) and DP1050-1 (purple). The black and cyan curves rise steeply and terminate below about 7 % strain, whereas orange DP1000-1 peaks highest among the long curves near 30 % strain (between the 1200 and 1350 MPa gridlines), and red DP1000-5 and purple DP1050-1 extend past 40 % strain at lower plateau stresses. (b) Scatter plot of SUTS (GPa·g⁻¹·cm³, 80-260) against TE (%, 0-60) for 2000 series Al alloys (orange squares), Ti6Al4V (dark-blue circles), austenitic steels (purple triangles), duplex steels (cyan diamonds) and 'Our steel' (red stars), with shaded ellipses per class and dotted contour lines labelled 2, 4, 6 and 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% marking the SUTS×TE product. Red stars labelled DP950-1, DP950-5, DP1000-1, DP1000-5-TD, DP1000-5 and DP1050-1 cluster at the top-right; DP1000-5 and DP1050-1 lie beyond the 8 contour. The two panels jointly argue that the designed duplex steel combines the highest strength-ductility-density product.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legible legend entries are DP950-1 (black), DP950-5 (cyan), DP1000-1 (orange), DP1000-5 (red solid line), DP1000-5-TD (dotted red line) and DP1050-1 (purple).
In (a) the y-axis is 'Engineering stress (MPa)' drawn with a broken axis (jump from ~450 to ~1050 MPa) and the x-axis is 'Engineering strain (%)' from 0 to 50 with break marks near 5 % and 48 %.
In (a) the black (DP950-1) and cyan (DP950-5) curves terminate at low strain (well left of the 10 % gridline), whereas the red (DP1000-5) and purple (DP1050-1) curves extend beyond the 40 % gridline.
In (a) the orange DP1000-1 curve shows the highest plateau stress among the long curves, peaking between the 1200 and 1350 MPa gridlines at roughly the 30 % strain gridline.
In (a) all curves yield continuously without a distinct yield-point drop, and the purple DP1050-1 curve has the lowest plateau stress of the long curves.

Panel (b) plots SUTS in GPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (y, 80-260) against TE in % (x, 0-60) and its legend classes are 2000 series Al alloy (squares), Ti6Al4V (circles), Austenitic steels (triangles), Duplex steels (diamonds) and 'Our steel' (stars).
In (b) dotted diagonal contour lines are labelled 2 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, 4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, 6 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% and 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, and the red stars for DP1000-5 and DP1050-1 lie beyond the 8 contour.

In (b) the six red stars are individually labelled DP950-1, DP950-5, DP1000-1, DP1000-5, DP1000-5-TD and DP1050-1, with DP950-1/DP950-5 at high SUTS but TE below the 10 % gridline and DP1000-5/DP1050-1 at TE near the 40-50 % gridlines.

The caption states that the contour lines in (b) indicate the product of SUTS and TE, ranged from 2 to 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³, and that SUTS and TE denote specific ultimate tensile strength and total elongation respectively (the caption omits the % unit shown on the contours).

The citing text states that DP950-1 has the highest ultimate tensile strength (UTS) but lowest TE, and that increasing the annealing time to 5 min decreased YS and UTS by about 90 MPa without improving ductility.

The citing text states that DP1000-5 and DP1050-1 have products of SUTS and TE of more than 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, whereas 2000 series Al alloys and Ti6Al4V fall below 4, duplex steels in the range 2.7-6.5 and austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels in the range 2.9-7.4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%.
The citing text states that the TD-tested specimen DP1000-5-TD has similar YS/UTS but lower TE than DP1000-5, which is consistent with its plotted position in (b) at lower TE than the DP1000-5 star.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (stress in MPa, 0-1500 with broken axis; strain in %, 0-50 with break marks) for six specimens: DP950-1 (black), DP950-5 (cyan), DP1000-1 (orange), DP1000-5 (red), DP1000-5-TD (dotted red) and DP1050-1 (purple). The two 950 °C curves terminate below ~7 % strain; the longer curves end beyond 40 % strain, with DP1000-1 reaching the highest stress of the long curves.

Scatter plot of SUTS (GPa·g⁻¹·cm³, 80-260) versus TE (%, 0-60) comparing 'Our steel' (red stars, labelled DP950-1, DP950-5, DP1000-1, DP1000-5, DP1000-5-TD, DP1050-1) with 2000 series Al alloy (orange squares), Ti6Al4V (dark-blue circles), austenitic steels (purple triangles) and duplex steels (cyan diamonds); shaded ellipses and dotted contour lines labelled 2, 4, 6 and 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% indicate the SUTS×TE product.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the black DP950-1 curve is largely overlapped by the cyan DP950-5 curve, so its peak stress and exact fracture strain cannot be read
panel (a): the dotted red DP1000-5-TD curve cannot be reliably separated from the solid red DP1000-5 curve
panel (b): no numeric coordinate labels are printed for any scatter point, so individual SUTS/TE values can only be estimated from gridlines
